column2: Retain divisions of gates, Koreim, Mosollamia son of Kore and descent from Abiasaph. The gate heading is not silently converted into a personal name or a different family.
Retain Zacharias firstborn, Idiel second, Zabadias third and Jethnouel fourth. Firstborn is distinct from the subsequent numerical ranks.
Retain Olam fifth, Joanan sixth and Elioenai seventh, completing Mosollamia's seven-name list without a newly supplied total.
Retain Abdedom's Samaias firstborn, Jozabad second, Joaa third, Sochar fourth and Nathanael fifth. The first five ranks continue into the next unit.
Retain Amiel sixth, Issachar seventh and Phollathi eighth, and God's blessing as the explanation. The blessing subject is God, not one of the sons.
Retain Samaia, sons of the firstborn Rosai, the ancestral house and their might. The selected Rosai expression is not replaced with a conventional rulers translation without evidence.
column3: The firstborn attachment and whether Rosai is a name or a borrowed designation remain unresolved; the inherited English is provisional.

column2: Retain Gothni, Raphael, Obed, Elzabad, Achiou, Eliou, Sabchia and Isbakom, with the mighty-sons phrase in its selected position. No entries are removed to match another roster.
column3: The exact grouping around Achiou and mighty sons remains a genealogical and punctuation question.

column2: Retain sons, brethren and sons of the descendants, their capable work and sixty-two for Abdedom. The count is not replaced by the sixty-eight in chapter 16.
Retain eighteen mighty sons and brethren for Mosollamia. This is the whole stated group, not eighteen added to the seven named sons.
Retain Osa of Merari, sons guarding the leadership, not firstborn and a father's making him ruler. The sentence continues into verse 11; no named firstborn or chief is imported.
column3: The unnamed he/him and the relation of guarding to the plural sons remain unresolved.

column2: Retain of the second division as continuation, Tablai third, Zacharias fourth and thirteen sons and brethren for Osa. Do not create a missing named second son to make a conventional roster.
Retain gate divisions, rulers of mighty men and service courses like their brethren in the Lord's house. The comparison concerns service rather than identity with the priestly courses.
Retain lots for small and great by ancestral houses and for each gate. Each gate conveys the repeated gate-and-gate expression without asserting identical staffing.
Retain the eastern lot for both Salamia and Zacharia, sons of Joas drawing for Melchia and a northern outcome. Do not substitute Zacharia alone as the northern recipient.
column3: The relationship of the sons of Joas to Melchia and the precise lot participants remain open.

column2: Retain Abdedom's south allocation opposite the house of esephin, with the sentence continuing into the next unit. No storehouse gloss is silently substituted for the opaque form.
column3: Esephin remains unapproved borrowed terminology; its building or institutional referent requires review.

column2: Retain for the second, Osa westward, the chamber-of-ascent gate and guard opposite guard. The difficult opening belongs to the selected sequence rather than a missing name reconstructed from another text.
column3: The connection of for the second and the precise gate/topographical arrangement remain unresolved.

column2: Retain six east daily, four north daily, four south daily and two for esephin. Do not double the final two or insert a second two from a parallel reading.
Retain the relieving personnel, four westward and two for the path relieving one another. The selected path and westward quantities are not reallocated to a conjectural Parbar building.
column3: The first relieving phrase's attachment to the previous verse and the distribution of the shifts require syntactic review.

column2: Retain the summary as gatekeepers' divisions of Kore's and Merari's sons. The earlier gate heading and this personnel heading remain distinct.
Retain Levites their brethren over both house treasuries and consecrated-thing treasuries. Do not replace brethren with a named Ahijah from another witness.
Retain the repeated Ladan/Gersoni descriptions and Jiiel under the plural ancestral-rulers heading. The repeated family expressions are not collapsed into a new simpler pedigree.
Retain Jiiel's Zethom and Joel as brethren over the house treasuries. The two named men share the assignment; no third custodian is supplied.
Retain the four-name heading Ambram, Issaar, Chebron and Oziel. The sentence remains introductory to the following treasury personnel.
Retain Soubael related through Gersam to Moses and leadership over the treasuries. Descendant is the inherited broad treatment of the genitive chain, not a demonstrated generational interval.
column3: Review whether son more accurately represents these relations; no genealogical generation is added or removed here.

column2: Retain his brother Eliezer, Raabias explicitly a son and the subsequent Josaias, Joram, Zechri and Salomoth. Do not insert repeated his son between names absent from this selected clause.
column3: The antecedent of his brother and the genealogical relation of the following names remain unresolved.

column2: Retain Salomoth and brethren over all consecrated treasuries, with David, ancestral rulers and military leaders as donors. The different command ranks remain explicit.
Retain singular he taking from wars and spoils and dedicating from them so that construction does not fall behind. Gifts supplies the implied consecrated objects; no new donor is named.
column3: The singular agent after the plural donors and the nuance of delaying or lacking for construction remain open.

column2: Retain Samuel the prophet, Saul of Kis, Abenner of Ner and Joab of Sarouia, and all their consecrations under Salomoth and brethren. The inherited descendant relations remain broad, not independently established generations.
Retain Issari Chonenia and sons for outside work, scribal activity and judgments over Israel. Outside is not expanded into foreign missions or a precise boundary absent from the clause.
Retain Chebroni Asabias with brethren, 1,700 mighty men, oversight west of Jordan and both divine ministry and royal work. West is selected and not corrected to east.

Retain Joudias as Chebroni ruler, the fortieth regnal year and a singular mighty man found at Jazer in Galaaditis. The inherited his reign refers contextually to the king rather than making Joudias a king.
column3: The distant regnal antecedent and the singular found man in relation to the next plural group require discourse review.

column2: Retain 2,700 mighty ancestral rulers appointed by David over Roubeni, Gaddi and half Manasseh. Their scope includes every ordinance of the Lord and word of the king, not only military tasks.

Retain ancestral rulers, thousand/hundred commanders and scribes serving the people and royal commands, monthly entry and exit and 24,000 in each division. Do not turn the monthly organization into a single simultaneous army total.
Retain first month, Jesboam son of Zabdiel and 24,000. The selected Jesboam is not harmonized with earlier warrior-list name forms.
Retain descent from Phares and leadership over all the first month's military rulers. This continues the description of Jesboam without introducing another commander.
Retain second month Dodia the Echochi, 24,000 and the trailing commanders of the force. No missing subordinate name is reconstructed.
column3: The attachment of the final plural commanders phrase remains uncertain; the inherited comma does not settle it.

column2: Propose placing priest and ruler directly after Banaias before son of Jodae. The selected nominative titles agree with Banaias, while Jodae belongs to the genitive parentage phrase. The old placement can misattach the offices to his father; the close stage preserves it. Third month and 24,000 remain unchanged.
Retain Banaias mightier than and over the thirty, followed by his son Amizabath over his division. No contradiction is removed by changing thirty to three or making Amizabath an unrelated commander.
Retain fourth month Asael, Joab's brother, his son Zabdias and the brethren, with 24,000. No after him succession clause is inserted for Zabdias.
Retain fifth month leader Samaoth the Jesrae and 24,000. The distinctive designation is not normalized from another warrior list.
Retain sixth month Odouias son of Ekkes the Thekoite and 24,000. Parentage and local designation remain attached to the named commander.
Retain seventh month Chelles from Phallous, Ephraimite descent and 24,000. The source's place form remains rather than a reconstructed ethnonym.
Retain eighth month Sobochai the Isathi, affiliation with Zarai and 24,000. Isathi is not silently harmonized to Ousathi elsewhere.
Retain ninth month Abiezer from Anathoth in Benjamin's land and 24,000. The territorial phrase is not reduced to immediate paternity.
Retain tenth month Meera from Netouphat, belonging to Zarai and 24,000. The selected Meera form remains provisional.
Retain eleventh month Banaias from Pharathon, Ephraimite descent and 24,000. This separate designation is not collapsed with third-month Banaias son of Jodae.
Retain twelfth month Choldai the Netophati, belonging to Gothoniel and 24,000. The completed sequence remains twelve monthly assignments.
Retain Reuben's Eliezer son of Zechri and Simeon's Saphatias son of Maacha. This begins tribal administration rather than continuing the monthly divisions.
Retain Levi's Asabias son of Kamouel and Aaron's Sadok as separate listed assignments. No inference that Aaron is another land tribe is added.
Retain Judah's Eliab among David's brethren and Issachar's Ambri son of Michael. Eliab is not changed to Elihu from another source.
Retain Zaboulon's Samaias son of Abdiou and Nephthali's Jerimoth son of Esriel. Both parentage relations remain distinct.
Retain Ephraim's Ose son of Oziou and half Manasseh's Joel son of Phadaia. This first half is not given an unexpressed geographical label.
Retain Galaad's half-Manasseh under Jaddai son of Zabdiou and Benjamin's sons under Asiel son of Abenner. The two halves of Manasseh remain separately represented.
Retain Dan's Azarael son of Joram and the tribal-head summary. No Gad or Asher entry is invented to complete an expected tribal roster.
Retain twenty years and downward excluded from David's numbering and the star-multiplication promise as rationale. The boundary is not silently rewritten as strictly under twenty.
Retain Joab beginning but not finishing, wrath upon Israel and non-registration in David's daily-record book. No denial that any partial number existed is added to reconcile chapter 21.
Retain Asmoth son of Odiel over royal treasuries and Jonathan son of Oziou over country, village, settlement and tower stores. The different locations are not compressed to cities alone.
Retain Esdri son of Choloub over those farming and working the land. The object is agricultural workers rather than merely a tract of property.
Retain Semei from Rama over estates and Zachri son of Sephni over wine stores in them. Estates is the selected general term; vineyards is not imported as the only land use.
Retain Balanas the Gedorite over olive groves and sycamores in the plain and Joas over oil stores. The two tree categories and separate storage appointment remain.
Retain grazing cattle in Asidon under Satrais the Sharonite and valley cattle under Sophat son of Adli. Asidon is not silently normalized to Sharon merely from the overseer's designation.
Retain Obil the Ishmaelite over camels and Jadias from Merathon over donkeys. Both origin labels and the distinct animals remain.
Retain Jaziz the Agarite over sheep and the summary of overseers of David's possessions. The summary covers the estate officials rather than only the last two animal keepers.

Retain Jonathan explicitly David's paternal uncle, counselor, understanding man and scribe, and Jiiel son of Achamani with the king's sons. Do not replace uncle with cousin to align another genealogy.
Retain Achitophel as counselor and Chousi as first friend. First is selected and is not dropped as if the phrase were merely a generic friendship.
Retain the difficult after-this-man/Achitophel sequence, Jodae son of Banaiou, Abiathar and Joab as chief commander. Do not reverse the Jodae/Banaias relationship to a more familiar patronymic.
column3: The placement of Achitophel and next in the selected syntax remains unresolved; the inherited fragment is not a settled reconstruction of succession.
